Listing those who had professed Islam at the Prophet's order, the companions count 1,500 and wonder whether they need fear, yet later trials force some to pray alone in fear.
To companions complaining of persecution, the Prophet recalled earlier believers sawn apart and combed with iron who kept their religion, and said Islam will prevail, but they are hasty.
Verse 22.11 describes a man who came to Medina and called Islam good when his wife bore a son and his mares foaled, and bad when they did not.
Every hardship, sickness or thorn-prick expiates a Muslim's sins; the believer bends under trials like a tender plant, and the Prophet suffered double fever for a double reward.
